requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to register my name, address and phone number, and optionally one bank account, so that the business knows who I am and can deliver my orders and contact me about them.

acceptance_criteria.text: A customer record holds a name, an address and a phone number, and each of these attributes is mandatory.
Given a customer record in which the name, the address or the phone number is absent, When the record is submitted, Then the system rejects the record and records no customer.
Given a customer record with a name, an address and a phone number, When the record is submitted, Then the system records the customer and the customer becomes known to the system.
A customer has at most one bank account, and the bank account is optional.
Given a customer record that contains no bank account, When the record is submitted, Then the system records the customer without a bank account.
Given a customer who already has a bank account, When a second bank account is added for that customer, Then the system rejects the addition and the customer keeps exactly one bank account.
A customer may have any number of orders, including none.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to browse the products on offer with their name, description, price and image, so that I can choose what to order.

acceptance_criteria.text: A product record holds a name, a description, a price and an image, and each of these attributes is mandatory.
Given a product record in which the name, the description, the price or the image is absent, When the record is submitted for storage, Then the system rejects the record and records no product.
Given a stored product, When the customer browses the products, Then the system shows the name, the description, the price and the image of that product.
The price of a product is a decimal number.
A product may be referred to by any number of order items, including none.
A product exists independently of the order items that refer to it and remains stored when an order item that refers to it is removed.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to submit an order for one or more products with a payment method of my choice, so that the business can fulfil my purchase.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a known customer, one or more order items each referring to an existing product, and a payment method, When the customer submits the order, Then the system registers an order with the submission date as its order date and the status submitted.
Given an order submission that names a customer not known to the system, When the submission is made, Then the system rejects the submission and registers no order.
Given an order submission that contains no order item, When the submission is made, Then the system rejects the submission and registers no order.
Given an order submission in which any order item refers to a product that does not exist, When the submission is made, Then the system rejects the submission and registers no order.
The total amount of a registered order equals the sum over its order items of quantity multiplied by unit price.
An order records an order date, a total amount, a status and a payment method, and each of these attributes is mandatory.
An order item records a quantity, a unit price and a reference to exactly one product, and each of these is mandatory.
An order contains one or more order items.
Each order item is associated with exactly one order.
An order item cannot be moved from the order it belongs to into another order.
An order item exists only as part of its order, and the order items of an order are removed when that order is removed.
Each order is associated with exactly one customer, and a customer may have any number of orders.
The unit price of an order item and the total amount of an order are decimal numbers.
The payment method of an order is one of bank, card or cash.
The status of an order is one of submitted, pending, filled, shipped or closed.
A newly registered order has the status submitted, from which the only permitted status change is to pending.

requirements.statement: As an Accountant, I want to raise an invoice for an order that has been filled, so that the customer is billed for the goods and the money owed can be collected.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order whose status is filled or shipped and that has no invoice, When the accountant raises an invoice with a date, an amount and a payment method, Then the system records the invoice against that order with the status issued.
Given an order that already has an invoice, When the accountant requests a further invoice for that order, Then the system rejects the request and records no further invoice.
Given an order whose status is submitted, pending or closed, When the accountant requests an invoice for that order, Then the system rejects the request and records no invoice.
Given an order that has been declined, When the accountant requests an invoice for that order, Then the system rejects the request and records no invoice.

Given an order whose status is filled and that has not been set to shipped, When the accountant raises an invoice for that order, Then the system records the invoice without requiring the order to have been shipped and leaves the status of the order at filled.
An invoice records a date, an amount, a status and a payment method, and each of these attributes is mandatory.
An order has at most one invoice, and each invoice is associated with exactly one order.
The amount of an invoice is a decimal number.
The payment method of an invoice is one of bank, card or cash.
The status of an invoice is one of issued or paid.
A newly raised invoice has the status issued, from which the only permitted status change is to paid.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to pay an invoice that has been issued to me, so that I settle what I owe for my order.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an invoice whose status is issued, When the customer submits a payment against it with a date, an amount and a payment method, Then the system records the payment against that invoice with the status pending.
Given an invoice whose status is paid, When the customer submits a payment against it, Then the system rejects the payment and records no payment.

Given an invoice whose earlier payment has the status failed, When the customer submits a further payment against that invoice, Then the system records the further payment as a separate payment with the status pending and keeps the earlier payment at the status failed.
A payment records a date, an amount, a status and a payment method, and each of these attributes is mandatory.
An invoice may have any number of payments, including none, and each payment is recorded against exactly one invoice.
A payment is recorded against an invoice and never directly against an order.
The amount of a payment is a decimal number.
The payment method of a payment is one of bank, card or cash.
The status of a payment is one of pending, completed or failed.
A newly submitted payment has the status pending, from which the only permitted status changes are to completed or to failed.

requirements.statement: As an OrderStaff, I want to receive a submitted order, so that it enters fulfilment and is not overlooked.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order whose status is submitted, When order staff receive the order, Then the system sets the status of the order to pending.
Given an order whose status is not submitted, When order staff attempt to receive the order, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the order unchanged.
Receiving an order changes its status only from submitted to pending.
Receiving never changes the status of an order whose status is closed.

requirements.statement: As an OrderStaff, I want to mark a pending order as filled once its goods have been assembled, so that it is ready to be shipped and invoiced.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order whose status is pending, When order staff mark the order as filled, Then the system sets the status of the order to filled.
Given an order whose status is not pending, When order staff attempt to mark the order as filled, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the order unchanged.
Marking an order as filled changes its status only from pending to filled.
Marking an order as filled never changes the status of an order whose status is closed.

requirements.statement: As an OrderStaff, I want to decline a pending order that cannot be fulfilled, so that it is closed without being shipped or billed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order whose status is pending, When order staff decline the order, Then the system sets the status of the order to closed.
Given an order whose status is not pending, When order staff attempt to decline the order, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the order unchanged.
Given an order that has been declined, When the accountant requests an invoice for that order, Then the system rejects the request and records no invoice.
Declining an order changes its status only from pending to closed.
A declined order keeps the status closed and its status is never changed again.

requirements.statement: As an OrderStaff, I want to set a filled order to shipped when it leaves for delivery, so that it is known that the goods are on their way to the customer.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order whose status is filled, When order staff set the order to shipped, Then the system sets the status of the order to shipped.
Given an order whose status is not filled, When order staff attempt to set the order to shipped, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the order unchanged.
Given an order whose status is filled and that has an invoice, When order staff set the order to shipped, Then the system leaves the status of that invoice and of every payment against it unchanged.

Given an order whose status is filled and that has no invoice, When order staff set the order to shipped, Then the system sets the status of the order to shipped without requiring an invoice to have been raised.
Shipping an order changes its status only from filled to shipped.
Shipping never changes the status of an order whose status is closed.

requirements.statement: As an Accountant, I want to confirm a pending payment once its money has been received, so that the invoice it settles is recorded as paid.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a payment whose status is pending, When the accountant confirms the payment, Then the system sets the status of the payment to completed.
Given a pending payment against an invoice whose status is issued, When the accountant confirms the payment, Then the system sets the status of that invoice to paid.
Given a pending payment against an invoice that bills an order, When the accountant confirms the payment, Then the system leaves the status of that order unchanged.
Given a payment whose status is not pending, When the accountant attempts to confirm the payment, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the payment unchanged.
Confirming a payment changes the status of the payment only from pending to completed.
Confirming a payment changes the status of its invoice only from issued to paid.

requirements.statement: As an Accountant, I want to reject a pending payment whose money has not been received, so that the invoice stays open and the customer can pay it again.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a payment whose status is pending, When the accountant rejects the payment, Then the system sets the status of the payment to failed.
Given a pending payment against an invoice that bills an order, When the accountant rejects the payment, Then the system leaves the status of that invoice and of that order unchanged.
Given a payment whose status is not pending, When the accountant attempts to reject the payment, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the payment unchanged.
Rejecting a payment changes its status only from pending to failed.

requirements.statement: As an OrderStaff, I want to close an order once it has been shipped and its invoice has been paid, so that completed orders are separated from those that still need attention.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order whose status is shipped and whose invoice has the status paid, When order staff close the order, Then the system sets the status of the order to closed.

Given an order whose status is shipped and whose invoice does not have the status paid, When order staff attempt to close the order, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the order unchanged.

Given an order whose invoice has the status paid and whose status is not shipped, When order staff attempt to close the order, Then the system rejects the attempt and leaves the status of the order unchanged.
A filled order is closed only after both the shipping of the order and the settlement of its invoice have completed, whichever of the two finishes last.
Closing an order changes its status only from shipped to closed.
An order whose status is closed is never changed again.

requirements.statement: The system shall register an order containing up to 50 order items and respond to its submission within 2 seconds for at least 95% of submissions under normal operating conditions.
The system shall support at least 200 concurrent users and at least 20 order submissions per second under normal operating conditions while meeting the response time of NFR-01.
The system shall authenticate every user before granting access to any customer, order, invoice or payment data, and shall reject 100% of unauthenticated requests.
The system shall allow only users holding the Accountant role to confirm or reject a payment, and shall reject 100% of such requests from users not holding that role.
The system shall encrypt customer personal data and bank account numbers in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher, and shall store them encrypted at rest.
The system shall record the user and the time of every status change of an order, an invoice and a payment, and shall retain each such record for at least 12 months.
The system shall be available for at least 99.5% of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least 24 hours in advance.
The system shall resume accepting requests within 15 minutes after a server failure without losing any order, invoice or payment recorded before the failure.
